context: An elderly couple reminisces about food
purpose: Teach: キリン/ハチ/蜂蜜/前菜/スイーツ/ガッツ/菜の花/リーフ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 動物園、子供たちと、キリン見たな、若い頃。
lines.en: I remember seeing giraffes at the zoo with the children, years ago.
lines.style: Quiet drift into memory. Slow, steady pace. Voice settles on the word 'giraffes' like a photograph he's holding. Gentle exhale underneath — no rush to fill the silence.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。庭のお花、毎年、ハチが来てくれるわ。
lines.en: Mmm. The flowers in the garden — the bees still come back every year.
lines.style: Soft agreement that blooms into its own thought. Slight smile in the voice. Warm observation, almost to herself. Pace gentle but not faltering.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 蜂蜜入りの紅茶、朝の楽しみ。
lines.en: Honey tea in the mornings — that's something I look forward to.
lines.style: Simple gratitude, spoken like a small ceremony. Soft attack. Each phrase rests on the one before it. The voice of someone who has learned to notice small things.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お料理、前菜から、丁寧に味わいたいわ。
lines.en: The meals themselves — I want to taste them properly, from the very first course.
lines.style: Wistful reach forward. Not quite regret, but the tender want of someone savoring what remains. Gentle insistence on 'properly.' Trailing softly at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い時、スイーツより、しょっぱい物が好きだった。
lines.en: When I was younger, I preferred savory things to sweets.
lines.style: Light, dry recognition — almost a small chuckle underneath. Matter-of-fact delivery that knows itself. No judgment, just the simple fact of change over time.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 子育ての日々、ガッツで乗り切ったわね。
lines.en: Those years raising the children — we got through them with pure determination.
lines.style: Strong, grounded voice. Not triumphant, but solid. A hand pat on the table. The quiet pride of someone looking back at hard work done well. Steady throughout.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 菜の花の畑、お前と歩いた春、忘れない。
lines.en: The canola flower fields we walked through that spring — I haven't forgotten that.
lines.style: Voice settles into deep memory. Long, tender pause before speaking. Slow pace, deliberate. The weight of a specific moment held carefully. Almost whispered at the close.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 紅茶リーフ、新しいの、明日試しましょう。
lines.en: Let's try those new tea leaves tomorrow.
lines.style: Gentle proposal, looking forward. Warm close to the conversation. Voice suggests a hand touching his arm. Simple, present, held in affection.
